topStories.headline: Record El Niño Tides Flood the Embarcadero, and Forecasters Warn the Season Has Only Just Begun
topStories.dek: Seawater overtopped Pier 14 and closed sidewalks along the waterfront this week as San Francisco's tidal gauge shattered its October record — twice.
topStories.body:
The Embarcadero flooded on a cloudless Monday afternoon, October 26, when seawater pushed onto the sidewalk south of the Ferry Building, cut off access to Pier 14, and rose through a storm drain along the roadway, prompting Port of San Francisco crews to cone off the area. It was the city's highest October tide on record — and that record was broken again on Tuesday, when tides peaked at 2.1 feet above the average daily high. By Thursday, water levels had climbed to 2.2 feet above normal, surpassing both October and November records.

The National Weather Service issued a coastal flood advisory that, as of Friday morning, remained in effect through the weekend. High tide at the San Francisco gauge was still expected to reach 1.9 feet above normal Friday afternoon and 1.5 feet above normal Saturday. The agency attributed the extraordinary readings to El Niño warming of Pacific coastal waters, which has pushed sea levels more than a foot above what annual tide charts predicted.

Port of San Francisco spokesperson Eric Young confirmed the connection to El Niño conditions. Caution tape went up along sections of the Embarcadero bike lane and sidewalk on Tuesday, and the public art installation 'Corpus' at Pier 14 was blocked off by flooding. Pedestrians gathered to photograph the water covering surfaces normally well above the waterline.

Experts are warning that this week's flooding may preview a far more disruptive winter. A coastal engineer working on a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Port of San Francisco proposal to protect the waterfront from long-term sea-level rise told the San Francisco Chronicle she expects tides high enough to shut the entire Embarcadero down. Port Executive Director Michael Martin identified the Muni Metro tunnel entrance near Pier 14 and the Agriculture Building just east of the Ferry Building as additional sites at high risk. Residents should check the NWS Bay Area coastal flood advisory page for updated tide forecasts before venturing to the waterfront.

topStories.headline: Two Outside Investors Have Quietly Assembled Seven Union Square Buildings — and Just Bought Their Latest
topStories.dek: Project Uris, the bet-on-San-Francisco vehicle run by Ian Jacobs and Max Raskin, closed on an eight-story office building at Post and Kearny streets on October 28.
topStories.body:
Uris Acquisitions purchased the eight-story office building at 47 Kearny Street — on the corner of Post and Kearny — for $4.2 million, or roughly $150 per square foot, according to The Real Deal and Hoodline. It was the building's first sale in more than four decades. The 28,660-square-foot property is 89 percent leased. The deal closed October 28 and was handled by Colliers brokers Julie Taylor and Darren Kuiper on behalf of the buyers.

The purchase is the seventh in a growing portfolio assembled under 'Project Uris,' an investment initiative that Ian Jacobs — a descendant of the Reichmann real estate family — launched in 2024 with New York-based partner Max Raskin. The duo initially raised $75 million, targeting distressed commercial properties across downtown San Francisco with a stated goal of acquiring 3 million square feet. According to the San Francisco Standard, the 47 Kearny deal and a simultaneous acquisition at 165 Post Street totaled $19.6 million, bringing their combined spending to roughly $50 million across seven properties spanning five retail corridors around Union Square.

Earlier purchases include the Art Moderne building at 200 Powell Street, 35 Powell Street, 111 Ellis Street, and a building on Maiden Lane. The investors have also involved themselves in the Union Square Alliance, and Raskin joined the board of Golden Gate University this year. The Standard noted that the retail scene around Union Square has improved markedly since the duo began buying — a recovery driven in part by the return of major national tenants — though the portfolio still represents a small fraction of Jacobs' long-term acquisition target.

topStories.headline: Italian Espresso-and-Pizza Kiosk La Piazza Wins Nine-Year Lease on Union Square's Most Contested Food Stand
topStories.dek: The family behind Colibri and Il Parco will open a grab-and-go Italian concept at the city-owned Powell Street kiosk that has sat idle since celebrity chef Tyler Florence vacated it in 2025.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Recreation and Parks announced on October 9 that it had selected La Piazza — an Italian espresso and pizza bar concept from the Rallo family, who also operate Colibri and Il Parco — for a nine-year lease on the city-owned kiosk on the western side of Union Square near Powell Street. The announcement ended a lengthy search for a new tenant after Tyler Florence's Miller & Lux Provisions departed the contentious space in 2025.

La Piazza plans to serve pizza, piadina, focaccia sandwiches, espresso drinks, and housemade pastries. The Rallos intend to open the kiosk in April 2027. The family previously operated Colibri, a Mexican restaurant that relocated from the Union Square area to the Presidio in 2022, giving them deep roots in the neighborhood. Recreation and Parks confirmed the new tenant will not receive city funding.

Mayor Daniel Lurie cited the selection as part of the administration's effort to accelerate downtown's recovery. The kiosk sits within the footprint of the Powell Street Improvement Project, which is directing public and private money toward street upgrades from the cable car turnaround up into Union Square. The Rallo family is also planning Il Porto, a quick-service Italian café, for Pier 31 on the northern Embarcadero, expected to open early next year.

events.title: Ferry Building Board Game Night
events.location: Ferry Building Marketplace, 1 Ferry Building, Embarcadero
events.description: Grab food or drinks from Ferry Building shops and stay to play classics like Scrabble, chess, and Monopoly, or try something new with games provided by Gamescape SF. Free to attend; games available in the public seating area between Book Passage and Cholita Linda.

events.title: Pickwick Vintage Show & Head West Marketplace at the Ferry Building
events.description: Two markets share the Ferry Building on the first Sunday of November: Pickwick Vintage brings over 40 local vendors of clothing, jewelry, and accessories to the Grand Hall (10 AM–4 PM), while Head West — a marketplace for emerging and established local brands — runs 11 AM–5 PM. Pickwick admission is $12; Head West is free.

events.title: Downtown First Thursdays with Big Freedia
events.location: 2nd Street between Market and Howard Streets, SoMa/East Cut
events.description: Downtown SF's free monthly street party returns for November with New Orleans bounce legend Big Freedia headlining at Howard and 2nd from 8–9 PM, plus DJs, drag performers, food trucks, and pop-up shopping across three blocks. Free entry; RSVP on Eventbrite for drink discounts at the outdoor bars.

events.title: Fall SF International Tea Festival
events.location: Ferry Building Marketplace, Second Floor Grand Hall, 1 Ferry Building, Embarcadero
events.description: The two-day festival features unlimited tastings from 30-plus tea makers — including established brands and local artisans — plus expert presentations and a souvenir porcelain tasting cup included with admission. Tickets start at $19 at sfitf.com.

moreNews.headline: Los Angeles Apparel Opens First SF Store at 111 Powell, Taking Over Former Uniqlo Space
moreNews.body: Los Angeles Apparel — the clothing brand founded by American Apparel's Dov Charney — confirmed in early October that it planned to open its first San Francisco location at 111 Powell Street in Union Square, moving into a space previously occupied by Uniqlo before that chain relocated down Market Street. The store, which opened in October, marks the brand's debut in the city. It lands at the heart of the Powell Street Improvement Project, which is directing public and private funds toward streetscape upgrades around the cable car turnaround and into Union Square Plaza.

moreNews.headline: Lids Expected Back at 50 Powell Street by November, Three Years After Closing
moreNews.body: Sports retailer Lids is set to return to Union Square with a new location at 50 Powell Street, expected to open in November 2026 according to building permits reported by the San Francisco Standard. The chain closed its previous Union Square store roughly three years ago. The comeback is part of a broader wave of national retailers re-signing leases in the neighborhood as foot traffic and retail vacancy rates improve.

restaurants.name: Wayfare Tavern
restaurants.description: Tyler Florence's relocated flagship—now in a grand four-room space at 201 Pine St—serves celebrated fried chicken, seasonal deviled eggs, and classic Victorian-era cocktails in a gold-leaf and tufted-leather setting.

restaurants.name: Tadich Grill
restaurants.description: California's oldest continuously operating restaurant, founded in 1849, still serving Croatian-style charcoal-broiled seafood and cioppino at its longtime California Street address.

restaurants.name: Perbacco
restaurants.description: Polished Piemontese and Ligurian cooking—agnolotti dal plin, pappardelle with short rib ragù, and an award-winning Italian wine list—in an upscale Financial District room.

restaurants.name: Benu
restaurants.description: Chef Corey Lee's three-Michelin-star restaurant near the Financial District serves a precise tasting menu blending Asian, American, and French traditions, open Wednesday through Saturday.

restaurants.name: Angler
restaurants.description: Michelin-starred Embarcadero waterfront restaurant from Saison Hospitality where every dish is touched by a 32-foot wood-burning hearth, serving premium seafood and steaks with bay views.

restaurants.name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
restaurants.description: Beloved Ferry Building oyster counter and casual dine-in restaurant serving sustainably farmed Tomales Bay oysters, craft cocktails, and a seasonal seafood menu with views of the Bay Bridge.

restaurants.name: Arquet
restaurants.description: The Ferry Building's newest full-service restaurant from the team behind Sorrel, open Wednesday through Sunday for lunch and dinner in the historic space formerly occupied by The Slanted Door.

restaurants.name: Bon Delire
restaurants.description: Kais Bouzidi's Parisian-inspired waterfront bistro near the Ferry Building, serving classic French fare with waterfront atmosphere along the Embarcadero.

restaurants.name: Waterbar
restaurants.description: Embarcadero waterfront restaurant serving fresh oysters, seafood, and California cuisine with dramatic floor-to-ceiling aquarium installations and views of the Bay Bridge.

restaurants.name: The Garden Court Restaurant
restaurants.description: San Francisco Landmark No. 18, this sky-lit dining room under Austrian crystal chandeliers inside the Palace Hotel serves elevated breakfasts and signature afternoon tea.

restaurants.name: Sisterita
restaurants.description: Locally sourced, casual-dining café in the Financial District earning top neighborhood ratings on Yelp for breakfast and lunch.

restaurants.name: Wayfare Tavern Bar
restaurants.description: The bar program at Wayfare Tavern's new Pine Street home features an expansive California-centric wine list alongside Victorian-era classic cocktails.

restaurants.name: Barbarossa Lounge
restaurants.description: Locally owned, walk-in-welcome cocktail lounge in the Financial District open late, known for a trendy, relaxed atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Kin Khao
restaurants.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand Thai restaurant inside the Parc 55 hotel near Union Square, serving unique, deeply layered flavors that diverge from typical Thai restaurant menus.

restaurants.name: Corzetti
restaurants.description: Union Square Italian restaurant popular for its $20 rotating lunch specials and fresh ingredients, with strong reviews for service and value.

restaurants.name: John's Grill
restaurants.description: A San Francisco institution open for over 116 years near Union Square, offering live music, classic American fare, and the setting immortalized in Dashiell Hammett's The Maltese Falcon.

restaurants.name: HINODEYA Ramen Union Square
restaurants.description: Casual, late-night ramen shop near Union Square with a broad menu and highly rated for quick, satisfying bowls.

restaurants.name: Nopa Fish
restaurants.description: 2025 Ferry Building newcomer operating as part casual restaurant, part retail fish market, featuring sustainably sourced California seafood in sandwiches, fish and chips, and seasonal small plates.

restaurants.name: Parachute Bakery
restaurants.description: Opened September 2025 in the Ferry Building by the culinary team behind Michelin-recognized Sorrel, offering melt-in-your-mouth pastries in one of the waterfront's most sought-after new spots.

restaurants.name: Roli Roti Gourmet Rotisserie
restaurants.description: Ferry Building market favorite serving slow-roasted Porchetta sandwiches, rotisserie chicken, and herb-roasted potatoes at the weekend farmers market and select weekday hours.

hotels.name: The Westin St. Francis San Francisco on Union Square
hotels.description: An iconic 1,195-room Union Square institution open since 1904, featuring turn-of-the-20th-century European elegance, Bourbon Steak restaurant, cable car access at the door, and a $45 million suite renovation.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco at Embarcadero
hotels.description: Michelin Two-Key hotel occupying floors 39–48 of a Financial District skyscraper, with sweeping Bay views, the Orafo restaurant, and a new seasonal sky-high pop-up bar on the 40th-floor terrace.

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
hotels.description: 821-room waterfront hotel at Embarcadero Center featuring a signature 17-story atrium lobby, recently renovated guest rooms, and Eclipse Kitchen & Bar overlooking the Financial District.

hotels.name: Palace Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel
hotels.description: San Francisco landmark since 1909, with a sky-lit indoor pool, 556 rooms, and two iconic dining venues—the crystal-chandeliered Garden Court and the celebrated Pied Piper Bar.

hotels.name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco Union Square
hotels.description: Situated directly on Union Square, this flagship hotel offers panoramic city views, easy cable car access, and proximity to Chinatown and the Financial District.

hotels.name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
hotels.description: Well-located full-service hotel in the heart of the Financial District, popular with business travelers for its comfortable rooms, professional staff, and on-site bar.

hotels.name: Handlery Union Square Hotel
hotels.description: Family-owned and operated since 1948, this Union Square hotel on Sutter Street offers one of the few outdoor pools in the neighborhood and consistently strong service reviews.

hotels.name: Beacon Grand, A Union Square Hotel
hotels.description: Highly rated Union Square boutique hotel earning top TripAdvisor value rankings with friendly staff and excellent city views.

hotels.name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
hotels.description: Top-rated value hotel directly on Union Square, consistently ranked among the best values in San Francisco with highly praised location and staff.

shops.name: Britex Fabrics
shops.description: A San Francisco institution since 1952, now at 117 Post Street, offering 8,000 square feet of hand-selected textiles, trims, and sewing supplies from around the world.

shops.name: Nintendo San Francisco
shops.description: The brand's flagship San Francisco store, opened in May 2025 at 331 Powell Street, offering Nintendo games, merchandise, and interactive experiences near Union Square.

shops.name: Macy's Union Square
shops.description: San Francisco's flagship Macy's department store anchoring Union Square, open for full-service shopping across multiple floors of fashion, beauty, and home goods.

shops.name: Anine Bing
shops.description: Danish-born designer Anine Bing's Jackson Square boutique, curated specifically for San Francisco's climate and style, offering women's clothing, shoes, bags, and accessories.

shops.name: Isabel Marant
shops.description: Award-winning French designer Isabel Marant's Jackson Square boutique offering men's and women's clothing and accessories, worn by international style icons.

shops.name: Filson
shops.description: Located in the historic Belli Building (built 1850) on Montgomery Street, Filson produces high-quality work and outdoor wear for both men and women.

shops.name: Shinola
shops.type: Watches, leather goods, and lifestyle boutique
shops.description: Detroit-based boutique watchmaker and leather goods shop nestled in the charming Hotaling Place alleyway in the heart of Jackson Square.

shops.name: The Epicurean Trader
shops.description: Ferry Building specialty grocer and wine shop with a well-curated selection of artisan cheeses, charcuterie, local provisions, and natural wines, beloved by locals and commuters alike.

shops.name: Ferry Plaza Wine Merchant
shops.description: Nearly 3,000-square-foot wine bar, bottle shop, and cheese destination inside the Ferry Building, offering wines from around the world and daily by-the-glass pours.

shops.name: FASHIONPHILE
shops.description: Union Square luxury resale boutique buying and selling authenticated pre-owned designer handbags, accessories, and jewelry.

shops.name: Recchiuti Confections
shops.description: San Francisco-born chocolatier with a Ferry Building location, handcrafting small-batch truffles and confections using premium cacao.

artEntertainment.name: Exploratorium
artEntertainment.description: World-renowned hands-on museum at Pier 15 on the Embarcadero, with 650+ interactive exhibits blending science, art, and human perception, open Tuesday–Sunday with adults-only After Dark Thursdays.

artEntertainment.name: Gallery Japonesque
artEntertainment.description: Jackson Square gallery curated by Koichi Hara featuring Japanese artists from ancient to contemporary, with a focus on stone sculpture, mixed-media work, and lithographs.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Arts Commission (SFAC) Galleries
artEntertainment.description: City-run galleries at three locations making contemporary Bay Area art accessible to broad audiences through curated exhibitions, with current shows running through January 2027.
artEntertainment.address: 1 Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Place (City Hall)

artEntertainment.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
artEntertainment.type: Historic landmark food hall and market
artEntertainment.description: The Embarcadero's 1898 Beaux-Arts landmark houses around 50 artisan shops and restaurants and hosts the celebrated Ferry Plaza Farmers Market on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays.

artEntertainment.name: Institute of Contemporary Art San Francisco
artEntertainment.description: Financial District contemporary art institution showcasing rotating exhibits of colorful and innovative works from local and international artists.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Railway Museum
artEntertainment.description: Free museum in the Financial District dedicated to the history of San Francisco's streetcars, cable cars, and rail transportation, featuring interactive exhibits and historic artifacts.

artEntertainment.name: Museum of San Francisco
artEntertainment.description: Opened in 2019 by the San Francisco Historical Society and housed in the first San Francisco Mint building, this Financial District museum focuses on the city's rich and layered history.

artEntertainment.name: Embarcadero Center Cinema
artEntertainment.description: Long-running Landmark Theatres cinema in Embarcadero Center 1, screening independent, foreign, and art-house films for Financial District audiences.

gymsRecreation.name: Embarcadero YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: Established 1908 YMCA branch at 169 Steuart Street in the Financial District offering a full gym, indoor pool, group fitness classes, and cardio equipment, open Monday–Saturday.

gymsRecreation.name: Equinox Pine Street
gymsRecreation.description: High-end Equinox gym in the Financial District offering a full range of cardio, strength, and group fitness equipment in a clean, professionally staffed facility.

gymsRecreation.name: Equinox Sports Club San Francisco
gymsRecreation.description: Full-service Union Square Equinox with extensive cardio equipment, weights, pools, and group fitness studios, catering to downtown professionals.

gymsRecreation.name: FITNESS SF – Transbay
gymsRecreation.description: Well-reviewed Financial District gym near the Transbay Terminal with consistently clean equipment, extensive cardio machines, and a welcoming staff.

gymsRecreation.name: FITNESS SF – Embarcadero
gymsRecreation.description: Embarcadero Center location of the locally owned FITNESS SF chain, with tons of equipment, clean facilities, and a top-rated manager team.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga – Fremont Street
gymsRecreation.description: Financial District yoga studio on Fremont Street near Salesforce Tower offering heated vinyasa, yoga sculpt, and functional strength classes timed to the downtown office schedule.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot 8 Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: LGBTQ-friendly hot yoga studio near Union Square, family-owned and highly rated for its notoriously heated rooms, welcoming community, and impeccably clean facilities.

gymsRecreation.name: Bay Club Financial District
gymsRecreation.description: Upscale Financial District athletic club offering outstanding service, top-quality gym equipment, and yoga studios including a space with Embarcadero views for sunrise sessions.

gymsRecreation.name: Embarcadero Plaza

gymsRecreation.name: Barry's FiDi
gymsRecreation.description: Financial District outpost of the internationally known Barry's bootcamp brand, offering treadmill-and-floor HIIT classes in a high-energy red-lit studio environment.
